rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadʿ here means headache: the drink does not cause their heads to ache.
rows.anchor: لا يصدعون عنها اي لا تصدع رؤوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Roman sūra, yaṣṣaddaʿūn means they divide or disperse.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى في سورة الروم يومئذ يصدعون اي يتفرقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣādiqūn means the prophets; the same wording in 5:119 refers to prophets whose faith is true.
rows.anchor: ليجزي الصادقين بصدقهم يعني النبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣādiqūn specifically means the emigrants.
rows.anchor: اولئك هم الصادقون يعني المهاجرين خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣādiqūn means those steadfast in jihad; a parallel applies the label to believers who have faith and strive.
rows.anchor: وكونوا مع الصادقين يعني في الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣādiqūn also means believers, and their ṣidq is their faith.
rows.anchor: ليجزي الله الصادقين بصدقهم يعني المؤمنين بإيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirr and ṣarṣar describe severe cold; the cited winds are cold and severe.
rows.anchor: مثل ما ينفقون في هذه الحياة الدنيا كمثل ريح فيها صر يعني شدة البرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣarra means persisting in a sin; the examples gloss it as continuing in shirk.
rows.anchor: ولم يصروا على ما فعلوا يعني ولم يقيموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarra means a cry or loud shout.
rows.anchor: فاقبلت امرأته في صرة يعني في صيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faṣurhunna ilayka means cut them up toward you.
rows.anchor: فصرهن اليك اي قطعهن اليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣirāṭ can mean a road or path; the cited examples include the path to Hell.
rows.anchor: ولا تقعدوا بكل صراط توعدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Fātiḥa, the straight path means the straight religion.
rows.anchor: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم يعني الدين المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basṭ can mean a bed or spread-out surface; Noah's verse describes the earth as bedding or a resting place.
rows.anchor: الرابع : البسط يعني به المهد والفرش كقوله تعالى في سورة نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basṭa means merit in knowledge and strength in the body.
rows.anchor: وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of stretching one's hands to water means reaching from a distance.
rows.anchor: إلا كباسط كفيه إلى الماء ليبلغ فاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣar can mean perception by the heart; people who do not see in these examples lack inward sight.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من ينظر إليك افانت تهدي العمى ولو كانوا لا يبصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīr means sight with the eyes; this sense also occurs in the account of Joseph and the description of sharp sight on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: فجعلناه سميعا بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baṣīr can mean possessing proof: Moses' interlocutor had proof in worldly life.
rows.anchor: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍāʿa can mean dirhams or money; Joseph's brothers find their money returned in their baggage.
rows.anchor: ولما فتحوا متاعهم وجدوا بضاعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍāʿa can mean goods, specifically cheese and clarified butter.
rows.anchor: الثاني : البضاعة متاع وهو الجبن والسمن . قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍāʿa can mean property or goods that can be used for gain.
rows.anchor: الثالث : البضاعة المال المنتفع به . قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biḍʿ denotes a number, here a number of years.
rows.anchor: الرابع : البضع العدد . قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry also lists two senses of baṭsh: punishment and strength.
rows.anchor: ب ط ش على وجهين العقوبة . القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firar means fleeing; flight cannot help if one flees from death or killing.
rows.anchor: ان فررتم من الموت او القتل يعني لا ينفعكم الهرب ان هربتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafirrun can mean to dislike or shrink from something; here it is death that people dislike.
rows.anchor: قل ان الموت الذي تفرون منه فانه ملاقيكم يعني الذي تكرهونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yafirru means to turn away and pay no attention to another person.
rows.anchor: يوم يفر المرء من اخيه يعني لا يلتفت اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firar can mean moving farther away or distancing oneself.
rows.anchor: فلم يزدهم دعائي الا فرارا يعني تباعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firāsh means a rug or bedding; the earth is described as a spread-out surface.
rows.anchor: هو الذي جعل لكم الارض فراشا يعني بساطا ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farāsh, with fatḥa on the first letter, means small locusts, described as neither flies nor mosquitoes.
rows.anchor: كالفراش المبثوث وهو طائر ليس بذباب ولا بعوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furush can mean elevated couches or ranks.
rows.anchor: وفرش مرفوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farsh or firāsh means sheep, and it is also said to mean camels too small to bear loads.
rows.anchor: ومن الانعام حمولة وفرشا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says ḥamūla are animals able to carry loads, while farsh are small animals unable to do so.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود والحمولة ما اطاق الحمل والفرش ما لم يطق وكان صغيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farḍ means to make obligatory: one makes the pilgrimage obligatory by entering consecration; it also describes prescribed marital rules and the amount one obligates oneself to pay.
rows.anchor: فمن فرض فيهن الحج يقول فمن اوجب فيهن الحج فاحرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farḍ can mean to explain or make clear; God made clear the expiation of oaths, as in the opening of the sūra of Light.
rows.anchor: قد فرض الله عليكم تحلة ايمانكم اي بين الله لكم تحلة ايمانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farḍ can mean to make permissible; God permitted what is described for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ما كان على النبي من حرج فيما فرض الله له يعني احل الله له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farḍ can mean to send down; this verse is said to be the only one neither Meccan nor Medinan, revealed at al-Juḥfa.
rows.anchor: ان الذي فرض عليك القرآن لرادك الى معاد يعني انزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damghānī says 28:85 is neither Meccan nor Medinan and was revealed at al-Juḥfa.
rows.anchor: ليس في القران اية لا مدنية ولا مكية غير هذه الاية نزلت بالجحفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farīḍa means the fixed inheritance allotment; the same phrase marks the obligatory distribution of alms.
rows.anchor: فريضة من الله يعني قسمة المواريث لاهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sanfarughu lakum means that God will keep watch over the two communities addressed.
rows.anchor: سنفرغ لكم ايها الثقلان اي سنحفظ عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afrigh means pour out; the examples ask for patience to be poured and molten metal to be poured over a wall.
rows.anchor: ربنا افرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fārigh means empty, though Moses' mother's heart was empty of all concern except concern for Moses.
rows.anchor: واصبح فؤاد ام موسى فارغا اي خاليا من كل هم الا هم موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-furqān can mean victory; the cited instance is explained as the Torah.
rows.anchor: اذ اتينا موسى الكتاب والفرقان يعني التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍaʿat means she gave birth; the same verb describes pregnant women giving birth when their term ends.
rows.anchor: قالت رب إني وضعتها أنثى والله أعلم بما وضعت يعني الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍaʿnā means we removed or lifted away a burden.
rows.anchor: ووضعنا عنك وزرك أي حططنا عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍʿ can mean setting something in place, as with the scales and the record.
rows.anchor: ونضع الموازين بالقسط ليوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍaʿa can mean spread or laid out: God spread the earth for creation.
rows.anchor: والارض وضعها للانام اي بسطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awḍaʿū means to travel or hasten along.
rows.anchor: ولأوضعوا خلالكم يبغونكم الفتنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍʿ can mean taking off clothes; the same usage appears in the rule about women setting aside outer garments.
rows.anchor: وحين تضعون ثيابكم من الظهيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍʿ can mean laying aside or being free of something, here putting down weapons, as when war lays down its burdens.
rows.anchor: أن تضعوا أسلحتكم أي تخلوا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waṭʾ can mean possession; the land not yet trodden is land not yet possessed.
rows.anchor: وأرضا لم تطئوها يعني لم تملكوها ستكون لكم دور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waṭʾ can mean killing; the believers might have killed people they did not know.
rows.anchor: لم تعلموهم أن تطئوهم يعني تقتلوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waṭʾ can mean passing through a place.
rows.anchor: ولا يطئون موطئا يغيظ الكفار يعني لا يمرون بمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waṭʾ means firmness or tranquility in the night vigil.
rows.anchor: هي أشد وطئا أي طمأنينة

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd reports the reading waṭāʾ, which he explains as better correspondence between ear and heart.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد وتقرأ أشد وطاء أي مواطأة للسمع والقلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waffā means he completed or fulfilled; Abraham fully carried out what was required of him.
rows.anchor: وابراهيم الذي وفى يعني أتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awfū means fulfilling a promise or covenant; the command to honor covenants parallels God's covenant with Israel.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep-time tawaffī means taking the mind: some sensory functions stop while other actions remain, including movement called seeing; the parallel describes souls taken in sleep and death.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل يعني عند النوم فيقبض الذهن وتتعطل بعض آلات الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffī of Jesus means God took him up to heaven, not that he died; Christians became Christians after his raising.
rows.anchor: فلما توفيتني كنت أنت الرقيب عليهم لأن النصارى تنصروا بعدما رفع عيسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffī can mean death: the angel of death takes the souls of people when they die.
rows.anchor: قل يتوفاكم ملك الموت الذي وكل بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birr means obedience and leaving disobedience.
rows.anchor: على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barran means obedient to one's parents, as also in Jesus' statement about his mother.
rows.anchor: أي مطيعا لوالدتي . وقال تعالى في سورة عبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barara means those obedient to God; the same sense applies to the record of the righteous.
rows.anchor: يعني مطيعين لله تعالى . كقوله تعالى في سورة المطففين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birr is piety reached through giving in charity what one loves.
rows.anchor: يعني حتى تبلغوا في الصدقة ما تحبون . وقال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the statement contrasting turning toward a direction with true birr, birr means faith.
rows.anchor: يعني الإيمان . وقال تعالى فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birr means taqwā, obedience to God and following Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعني بالتقوى أي طاعة الله تعالى وإتباع محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bariqa means the eye stared or became astonished.
rows.anchor: برق أي شخص ويقال عجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barq can mean lightning; the same word is used for lightning in several other verses.
rows.anchor: الثاني : البرق بعينه . قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the lightning in the example as Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : البرق الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basṭ means striking: the angels stretch their hands to strike the souls of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أي ضاربو أيديهم إلى أرواح الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basṭ means expansion or abundance; God expands provision for whom He wills.
rows.anchor: أي وسع . كقوله تعالى في سورة الرعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basṭ can mean opening one's hand; the command is not to open it completely, and God's hands are described as open.
rows.anchor: أي لا تفتح يدك . كقوله تعالى في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khusran means decrease or short-weighting; the command is not to reduce the measure, as in the verse about buyers receiving less.
rows.anchor: يقول ولا تنقصوا الميزان كقوله تعالى في سورة المطففين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khāsirūn can mean those who incur punishment because of their actions.
rows.anchor: في العقوبة - أي بسببها - كقوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushūʿ can mean humility; the verse says the duty is difficult except for the humble.
rows.anchor: يعني المتواضعين الثاني : الخشوع يعني الخوف فذلك قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushūʿ can mean fear; they were fearful of God.
rows.anchor: يعني خائفين الثالث : الخشوع سكون الجوارح ورمي البصر إلى موضع السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In prayer, khushūʿ is stillness of the limbs and directing one's gaze to the place of prostration.
rows.anchor: الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushūʿ can mean abasement or humiliation, as with voices lowered before God and humbled faces.
rows.anchor: يقول ذلت كقوله تعالى في سورة الغاشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāṭiʾūn can mean sinners whose sin is not shirk.
rows.anchor: خاطئون من غير شرك فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāṭiʾūn can mean sinners guilty of shirk; the same applies to the people who do not eat from the tree in Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني مذنبين في شرك وقال تعالى في سورة الحاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhaṭaʾnā means making an unintentional mistake.
rows.anchor: الخطأ الذي لم يتعمد ونحوه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhaṭṭuf can mean driving people away or taking them captive.
rows.anchor: التخطف بمعنى الطرد قوله تعالى في سورة الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭf can mean seizing or snatching something furtively; the bird snatches its prey in the other example.
rows.anchor: أي اختلس خلسة وقوله تعالى في سورة الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭfa can also refer to the act of snatching itself, as the lightning nearly snatches their sight.
rows.anchor: الثالث : الخطفة بعينها قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khafīf means light or easy; the pregnancy was easy.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : الخفيف الهين قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khifāfan can mean young, and is also said to mean having little property.
rows.anchor: الثاني : خفافا يعني شبانا ويقال : خفافا من المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhfīf means making something easier or gentler for you.
rows.anchor: الثالث : التخفيف التيسير قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhfīf can mean reducing punishment, here a request to ease one day of torment.
rows.anchor: الرابع : التخفيف نقصان العذاب قوله تعالى في سورة حم المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiffa can mean lightness in weight, as when the scales weigh light.
rows.anchor: ومن خفت موازينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khafiya means concealed or secret; the other examples describe hidden supplication, what is secret, and what has not yet come to be.
rows.anchor: فوجه منهما : خفي بمعنى أسر قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhfīhā can mean make it manifest or bring it out.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أخفى أي أظهر قوله تعالى في سورة طه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhlada can mean inclining toward something; he leaned toward the pleasures of earthly life.
rows.anchor: فوجه منهما : أخلد بمعنى مال قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhlada can also mean making someone immortal or everlasting.
rows.anchor: يحسب أن ماله أخلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujūd can mean bowing; the command to enter the gate prostrating is glossed as entering while bowing.
rows.anchor: يعني ركعا ومثلها في سورة البقرة كقوله تعالى في سورة النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujūd can mean literal prostration, as in the command to prostrate to God and worship Him.
rows.anchor: السجود بعينه قوله تعالى في سورة النجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 2:114, God's masājid specifically refers to the Temple in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: ومن أظلم ممن منع مساجد الله أن يذكر فيها اسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masājid can refer to the Sacred Mosque in Mecca; the passage about pilgrimage service cites it by name.
rows.anchor: الثاني : المساجد المسجد الحرام قوله سبحانه في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosque founded on piety refers to the Mosque of Qubāʾ.
rows.anchor: الثالث : المسجد مسجد قباء قوله تعالى في سورة التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masjid can refer to the Mosque of Harm, the mosque built to cause harm and disbelief.
rows.anchor: الرابع : المسجد مسجد الضرار قوله تعالى في سورة التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masājid can mean all the mosques where God's name is often remembered.
rows.anchor: لهدمت صوامع وبيع وصلوات ومساجد يذكر فيها اسمه الله كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masājid can mean the bodily parts used in prostration: forehead, nose, hands, knees, and feet.
rows.anchor: السادس : المساجد أعضاء السجود قوله تعالى في سورة الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Masjid al-Ḥarām can refer to Mecca itself.
rows.anchor: السابع : المسجد مكة قوله تعالى في سورة الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāḥir can mean a learned person.
rows.anchor: فوجه منها : السحر العلم قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siḥr can mean a lie; the same sense explains the description of an ongoing magic as a lie.
rows.anchor: الثاني : السحر الكذب قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Siḥr can mean optical illusion or taking people's eyes.
rows.anchor: الثالث : السحر الأخذ بالعين قوله تعالى في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masḥūr can mean mad or possessed; the heading also lists turning people away from truth as a sense of siḥr.
rows.anchor: الرابع : المسحور المجنون قوله تعالى في سورة الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry lists five senses of siḥr, including turning away from truth.
rows.anchor: س ح ر على خمسة أوجه العلم الكذب الأخذ بالعين الجنون الصرف عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurb can mean sexual intercourse; the command not to approach wives until purified means not to have intercourse with them.
rows.anchor: ولا تقربوهن حتى يطهرن أي لا تجامعوهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb means responsive: God is near in the sense of answering those who call upon Him.
rows.anchor: وإذا سألك عبادي عني فاني قريب أجيب دعوة الداعي إذا دعان أي مجيب لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb can mean near in time, here an impending punishment within three days; the Hour and the true promise are also said to have drawn near.
rows.anchor: فيأخذكم عذاب قريب يعني إلى مدة ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqrab can mean more correct or sounder.
rows.anchor: لأقرب من هذا رشدا أي لأصوب من هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqrab in affection means gentler in affection and speech.
rows.anchor: ولتجدن أقربهم مودة للذين آمنوا الذين قالوا إنا نصارى يعني ألينهم مودة وقولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurbā and qurba mean kinship or relatives.
rows.anchor: قوله سبحانه في سورة حم عسق إلا المودة في القربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearby place from which the caller calls is the rock in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: واستمع يوم ينادي المنادي من مكان قريب يعني من الصخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repenting min qarīb means repenting before death and seeing death; repentance is not accepted once death is witnessed.
rows.anchor: ثم يتوبون من قريب يعني قبل الموت والمعاينة ولا تقبل التوبة مع المعاينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought Moses near by speaking to him intimately and honoring him.
rows.anchor: وقربناه نجيا أي كلمناه من قريب إكراما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb can mean nearby, as in the threat that punishment might befall close to their homes.
rows.anchor: أو تحل قريبا من دارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurbān means an offering that draws one near to God.
rows.anchor: القربان القرب إلى الله تعالى قوله سبحانه في سورة المائدة إذ قربا قربانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurb can mean eating: the command not to approach the tree means not to eat from it.
rows.anchor: ولا تقربا هذه الشجرة يعني لا تأكلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurb can mean entering into an activity; not approaching prayer means not entering prayer while intoxicated.
rows.anchor: لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى يقول لا تدخلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīb can mean already present or imminent.
rows.anchor: إنا أنذرناكم عذابا قريبا يعني كائنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqarr is women's wombs and mustawdaʿ is men's loins, where the drop is deposited.
rows.anchor: مستقر يعني أرحام النساء ومستودع أصلاب الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqarr is where animals settle at night, while mustawdaʿ refers to their death.
rows.anchor: مستقر ومستودع حين هدوء الدواب بالليل ومستودع حين الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mustaqarr can mean an endpoint or final destination; examples use it for the sun, a report, and every affair.
rows.anchor: الثالث المستقر المنتهى قوله تعالى في سورة يس والشمس تجري لمستقر لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāriʿa can mean a raiding party or military detachment.
rows.anchor: تصيبهم بما صنعوا قارعة أو تحل قريبا من دارهم يعني سرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qāriʿa can mean the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى في سورة القارعة القارعة ما القارعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aqsatū means act justly; muqsiṭūn are the just.
rows.anchor: وأقسطوا إن الله يحب المقسطين يقول اعدلوا إن الله يحب العادلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāsiṭūn means those who are unjust and deviate from the truth.
rows.anchor: وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا يعني الجائرين المائلين عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīn can mean a helper or companion; the verse calls Satan an evil companion.
rows.anchor: ومن يكن الشيطان له قرينا فساء قرينا يعني فبئس القرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarīn can mean the recording angel who writes a person's deeds for and against them.
rows.anchor: القرين الكاتب له وعليه قوله تعالى في سورة ق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry's remaining listed faces associate qarīn with Satan and with a paired one or owner.
rows.anchor: على أربعة أوجه القرين المعين الكاتب الشيطان المقرن المالك
